newsitem.title: CHINA: Bad property deals brought down China Agribusiness.
newsitem.headline: Bad property deals brought down China Agribusiness.

text.p: High risk investments in real estate were to blame for the collapse of China Agribusiness Development Trust and Investment Corp (CADTIC) earlier this year, central bank vice governor Chen Yuan said on Wednesday.
Authorities had basically clarified the factors involved in the company's collapse, Chen told Reuters, adding that securities investments were not a major part of the firm's problems.
"They made high risk investments in real estate," he said, speaking after an international securities conference in Beijing.
Asked if there would be legal cases linked to any of those involved at China Agribusiness, an investment house under the Ministry of Agriculture, he said that was up to the judicial system to decide.
He said, however, that violations of regulations had taken place but did not elaborate.

CADTIC, one of China's largest investment trust houses, was closed on January 4 amid reports of enormous losses that had left the firm unable to repay debts. Its management had been handed over to the China Construction Bank. CADTIC had reported assets of about 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion).
